actual_rim_geometry.caliper_width_geometry: XY convex contact envelope, not the actual opening
actual_rim_geometry.scope: Finite contact-trial search envelope. A connected separated spatial rim and its convex shadow do not establish a free aperture, empty interior, or safe passage; native contact and unchanged final containment remain required.

extra_lower_bear_left_5mm_sweep.model_scope: continuous frozen tetrahedral body versus MuJoCo convex collision solids
limitations: Does not predict deformation, friction, grasp retention or contact forces.
Robot convex envelopes can overestimate nonconvex native collision surfaces.
Left pose is fixed at measured q; native affine compliance and future tracking are not included.
Only the declared straight translation segment is certified; other segments and obstacles require separate gates.
The certificate is for frozen-shape Cartesian translation, not continuous FK tracking of an interpolated joint trajectory.
A fresh actual-shape check remains necessary after physical preparation.

limits: All extra lowering and subsequent poses/shapes are CPU kinematic or frozen-shape hypotheses; no physical state is resumed or fabricated as observed.
A future 20/30 mm entry hand-clearance policy starts from pre-entry actual geometry; after deformation it may not equal this simple extra 10/20 mm endpoint translation.
All original commanded quaternion components are retained. Rigid clearance and tracking are sampled at 401 points; joint positions use continuous cubic extrema and rate retiming.
Bear-left gap is a continuous frozen tetrahedron translation certificate for all actual left collision solids. It does not certify evolving cloth/teddy contact or grip.
Diagnostic paths may continue beyond an earlier rejected segment to identify other obstacles; such continuation does not authorize execution.
Force, strain, grasp retention, final physical containment, contact during finger release/withdrawal and settled success require a fresh native full run.
